issues.title: Missing semicolons and single quotes used
issues.description: The rule requires using double quotes and always including semicolons, but the code uses single quotes for imports and omits semicolons after import statements and method calls
issues.rule_name: Use Biome for Code Formatting with Standardized Configuration

issues.title: Inconsistent date filter causes missing bookings in recurring event cancellation
issues.description: When cancelling recurring bookings with 'allRemainingBookings' flag, the code updates bookings using 'new Date()' as the time threshold but then fetches updated bookings using 'bookingToDelete.startTime'. This creates a time window mismatch where bookings between these two timestamps will be cancelled in the database but won't be included in 'allUpdatedBookings', causing workflow reminders and calendar event cleanup to be skipped for those bookings. This leads to orphaned reminders and stale calendar events that were cancelled but never properly cleaned up.

issues.title: Missing return value breaks caller's count tracking
issues.description: The 'updateMany' method in BookingRepository no longer returns the Prisma update result object which contains the count of updated records. According to the IBookingRepository interface, this method should return 'Promise<{ count: number }>', but the implementation now returns 'Promise<void>'. This breaks any calling code that depends on knowing how many bookings were updated, potentially affecting audit logging, metrics, or conditional logic that needs to verify if the update affected any records.

issues.title: Missing locale field causes translation failure in cancellation flow
issues.description: The 'userSelect' object used by UserRepository.findById (and subsequently findByIdOrThrow) no longer includes the 'locale' field. However, in handleCancelBooking.ts, the code calls 'getTranslation(organizer.locale ?? "en", "common")' which expects the locale property on the organizer object. Since locale is now undefined, the translation will always fall back to 'en' regardless of the user's actual locale preference, causing cancellation emails and notifications to be sent in the wrong language for non-English users.

issues.description: Three new repository files in apps/api/v2 use dot-suffix naming pattern (.repository.ts) which violates Rule #1 of the compliance rules. pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #24159 - chore: [Booking Cancellation Refactor - 2] Inject repositories and use them instead of Prisma in cancellation flow
pr.author: unknown

structured_output.summary:
This PR moves the booking cancellation flow (`handleCancelBooking.ts`) off direct Prisma calls and onto injected repositories: `UserRepository`, `BookingRepository`, `ProfileRepository`, `BookingReferenceRepository`, and a new `PrismaBookingAttendeeRepository`. It wires them through a new Nest provider set in `apps/api/v2` and through the `packages/features/di` container. The direction is right, and the duplicate `onBookingCancelled` call from the last revision is gone (I confirmed a single call remains).

The implementation has problems that would block merge. The new DI module imports a path that does not exist, so loading the cancel service container fails. `organizer.locale` is read after the PR removes `locale` from the shared `userSelect`, which breaks the type check and silently reverts organizer-facing emails to English. The bulk-cancel `findMany` filter changed from `new Date()` to `bookingToDelete.startTime` without being called out, which changes which bookings get reported as cancelled and which have their workflow reminders deleted. `BookingRepository.updateMany` does not match its interface's return type. The new tests only check `success` and `bookingId`, so they would pass even if the refactor deleted nothing.
structured_output.verdictRationale: One critical defect: `BookingReferenceRepository.module.ts` imports `@calcom/lib/server/repository/bookingReference`, which does not exist in the tree, and `BookingCancelService.module.ts` imports that module, so the DI container cannot load. Three high-severity issues follow: the removed `locale` select breaks the organizer translation and the type check, the recurring-cancel `findMany` filter drifted from the `updateMany` filter, and `BookingRepository.updateMany` does not satisfy `IBookingRepository`. The new tests also don't verify the behavior the refactor is meant to preserve.

architecture.overview:
Before this PR, `BookingCancelService` in `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts` took a `prismaClient` and called `prisma.*` directly throughout `handler`. The API v2 app (`apps/api/v2/src/lib/services/booking-cancel.service.ts`) subclassed it and injected `PrismaWriteService.prisma`. The DI container in `packages/features/bookings/di/BookingCancelService.module.ts` used a single `prismaClient` dependency.

This PR changes the service's dependency set to five repositories (user, booking, profile, booking reference, attendee) and adds a `dependencies ||` fallback in `handler` that builds the same repositories from the global `prisma` client. The API v2 layer gets new Nest providers that wrap the platform-library repositories. The DI container gets new per-repository modules. `BookingRepository` is extended with cancellation-specific query methods, and `ProfileRepository` gains an instance constructor and `findFirstByUserId`.
steps: Entry point: the API v2 `BookingCancelService` (apps/api/v2/src/lib/services/booking-cancel.service.ts) extends the platform-library base class and used to pass a Prisma client into `super`. It now passes five repository instances built by Nest from `BookingCancelModule`.

Wiring: `BookingCancelModule` (apps/api/v2) provides the new `Prisma*Repository` wrappers. Each wrapper extends a class exported from `packages/platform/libraries/repositories.ts`. The DI container path is `packages/features/bookings/di/BookingCancelService.module.ts`, which loads the repository modules through `depsMap`.

Service class: `BookingCancelService.handle` in `handleCancelBooking.ts` now calls `handler(input, this.deps)`. `handler` falls back to building repositories from the global `prisma` if no deps are passed. The default export is still `handler`, which is what the tests call.

Query moves: user, profile, and booking queries in `handler` now go through repository methods. Bulk recurring cancellation uses `findManyIncludeWorkflowRemindersAndReferences` and single cancellation uses `updateIncludeWorkflowRemindersAndReferences`, both on `BookingRepository`. Attendee deletion and reference soft-delete go through the attendee and booking-reference repositories.

Review hotspots: the `gte` filter in the recurring branch, the `organizer` select shape (no `locale`), the `updateMany` return type, and the broken import in the reference DI module. These are where the refactor changes behavior or breaks compilation.

findings.title: DI reference module imports a nonexistent path, breaking container load
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/bookings/di/BookingReferenceRepository.module.ts`, line 3 imports `BookingReferenceRepository` from `@calcom/lib/server/repository/bookingReference`, which does not exist. Change the import to `@calcom/features/bookingReference/repositories/BookingReferenceRepository`, the path `handleCancelBooking.ts` already uses. Then confirm that `BookingCancelService.module.ts` loads and that the type check passes.

findings.title: `organizer.locale` is no longer selected, breaking the translation and the type check
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/users/repositories/UserRepository.ts`, the PR removed `locale: true` from the shared `userSelect`. `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts` (around lines 337 and 370) reads `organizer.locale`, which is now missing from the type and `undefined` at runtime, so organizer emails fall back to English. Restore `locale` in the lookup used by the cancellation flow. Prefer adding it back to `userSelect` only if other callers are unaffected. Otherwise, select it explicitly for the organizer. Verify the type check passes and the organizer locale reaches `getTranslation`.

findings.title: Recurring-cancel `findMany` filter no longer mirrors the `updateMany` filter
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts`, the recurring branch (around lines 497-521) has an `updateMany` filtering on `startTime.gte = cancelSubsequentBookings ? bookingToDelete.startTime : new Date()`. The `findManyIncludeWorkflowRemindersAndReferences` call that follows uses `gte: bookingToDelete.startTime`, which the PR changed from `new Date()` without explanation. Compute the `gte` value once and use the same value for both calls, matching the original semantics: when `cancelSubsequentBookings` is false, the set of returned bookings should match what was just updated. Add a test that covers `allRemainingBookings` with a past instance so the behavior is pinned.

findings.title: `BookingRepository.updateMany` return type doesn't match `IBookingRepository`
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/bookings/repositories/BookingRepository.ts` around line 1502, `updateMany` has no `return` and is mis-indented. `IBookingRepository.updateMany` in `packages/lib/server/repository/dto/IBookingRepository.ts` declares `Promise<{ count: number }>`. Make the implementation `return await this.prismaClient.booking.updateMany(...)`, fix the indentation to match the class, and confirm the `implements` check passes. If the count is not wanted, change the interface to `Promise<void>` instead, and keep the two in sync.

findings.title: New tests don't verify the refactored side effects
findings.body:
The three new tests assert only `result.success`, `result.onlyRemovedAttendee`, and `result.bookingId`. None of them checks the DB or the side effects this refactor is about:

- The seated test never checks that attendees were deleted (`attendeeRepository.deleteManyByBookingId`).
- The recurring tests never check that the instances were cancelled or which ones were reported to `onBulkBookingsCancelled`. That is exactly the `gte` change above, which these tests would not catch.
- The "booking reference cleanup" test seeds two references but never checks that they were marked `deleted: true`.

The tests also call the default export, which is `handler` with no deps. That exercises the fallback path, not the injected repositories the PR introduces, so the DI wiring has no test. There are also no unit tests for `PrismaBookingAttendeeRepository`, `updateManyByBookingId`, or `ProfileRepository.findFirstByUserId`.

::diff{file="packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking/test/handleCancelBooking.test.ts" lines="1056-1063"}

::callout{type="warning"}
These tests would still pass if the refactor deleted every attendee and every reference. They give false confidence in exactly the risk the PR calls out.

Add assertions on observable state after `handleCancelBooking` (attendee count, `bookingReference.deleted`, booking status for each recurring instance). Add at least one test that goes through the `BookingCancelService` with explicit deps so the DI path is covered.
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking/test/handleCancelBooking.test.ts`, the three new tests (seated, recurring `allRemainingBookings`, booking reference cleanup) only assert `success`, `onlyRemovedAttendee`, and `bookingId`. Extend them to assert the observable side effects: attendees removed for the seated case, every affected recurring instance marked CANCELLED, and the seeded references marked `deleted: true`. Also add one test that constructs `BookingCancelService` with explicit repository deps, so the injected path is exercised and not just the `handler` fallback. Follow the existing assertion style in this file.

findings.title: Dual-path handler silently rebuilds repositories when deps are missing
findings.body:
`handler` takes an optional `dependencies` argument and falls back to constructing five repositories from the global `prisma` when it is missing. The service always passes `this.deps`, so production calls take the injected path, while the default export (used by tests and any other importer) takes the fallback.

The PR asks reviewers to check that the two paths stay in sync. Right now they are two parallel constructions of the same objects. The fallback is also where the `organizer` and `locale` issues above can diverge silently. Nothing forces the fallback and the DI path to change together.

::code{file="packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts" lines="139-152"}

The fallback is documented as a transition aid, but there is no TODO or removal ticket. Prefer making `dependencies` required on the internal `handler` and keeping the fallback only in the exported default, with a comment naming when it goes away.
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts`, `handler` (around lines 139-152) builds its repositories from the global `prisma` when `dependencies` is omitted. The `BookingCancelService` always passes deps, so the two paths can diverge. Move the default-construction into the exported default wrapper, make `handler` take required deps, and add a TODO referencing the follow-up that removes the default export. Do not change behavior for the service path.

findings.title: Inconsistent style and naming in the new repository and DI files
findings.fixPrompt: Run the repo formatter and linter on the files this PR touches. In `packages/features/bookings/repositories/PrismaBookingAttendeeRepository.ts`, switch to double quotes and semicolons to match the package. In `packages/features/bookings/di/BookingCancelService.module.ts`, use the `@calcom` alias instead of the relative import of `../lib/handleCancelBooking`. Revert unrelated re-indentation in `handleCancelBooking.ts` (the `team` spread block) and in `ProfileRepository.ts` so the diff shows only functional changes.

findings.title: Duplicate `onBookingCancelled` call from the last revision is fixed
findings.body: The PR description says a duplicate `bookingEventHandlerService.onBookingCancelled` call was removed. I checked `handleCancelBooking.ts` and there is now a single call, in the non-recurring branch, so the audit event fires once per cancellation. Good catch in the last revision.

findings.title: Shared dependency shape and wiring are consistent across the layers
findings.body: The new per-repository DI modules (`BookingAttendeeRepository.module.ts`, `BookingReferenceRepository.module.ts`, `Profile.module.ts`) follow the same `bindModuleToClassOnToken` + `moduleLoader` pattern as the rest of `packages/features/di`. `BookingCancelService.module.ts` and the API v2 provider list use the same five keys (`userRepository`, `bookingRepository`, `profileRepository`, `bookingReferenceRepository`, `attendeeRepository`), so the names don't drift between layers. The `BookingReferenceRepository` and `ProfileRepository` constructors keep their existing static methods, and I found no other `new ProfileRepository()` callers to break.

findings.title: Narrowed `workflowReminders` select is safe for the downstream consumer
findings.body: The new select returns only `id`, `referenceId`, and `method` for `workflowReminders`, instead of the full `WorkflowReminder` row. I checked `WorkflowRepository.deleteAllWorkflowReminders`, which takes exactly those three fields, so the narrowing is safe. The `updatedBookings` type was also narrowed to match.

findings.title: Replacing `uid ? {uid} : {id}` with the stored uid is safe
findings.body: The `where` clause now always uses `bookingToDelete.uid`, which is the row the handler has already loaded. In `schema.prisma`, `Booking.uid` is `String @unique`, so it is never null and always identifies the same row the old `{ id }` lookup did. This is a sound simplification and it removes a branch that could drift from the loaded booking.
